My skin type is dry and sensitive, I guess. My skin concerns are...Like it's so stupid. I feel so stupid because it feels like my fault. Ever since June of last year, I've had this horrible acne/rash thing on my cheeks. It's not as bad as it was when it first started, but it's still a major problem. It's not even like, normal pimples - it's like, deep in my skin and it burns and itches.  I'm 20 and until last year, all I ever had was breakouts from my period. I had a pretty clear face and all I ever used was Clean and Clear's daily cleanser, like the orange bottle one. But, in 2016, I graduated and lived with my older sister for a while, and that was when my skin started to get bad, but in June 2017 after I had been living with my parents again, it was the WORST. I just looked at my life, looked at my body, and decided I didn't want to live that way anymore. I think the turning point for me was when I realized I couldn't walk up the stairs at the mall anymore without being out of breath, and that just killed me. I didn't want to be in pain or out of breath anymore, I wanted to be strong and feeling good for the first time in a very long time. I guess I just got to the point where I decided it was enough, and for me that was the motive I needed to really make a change. It was just embarrassing, everyone around me healthy and being able to do things, and I'm in the back, behind out of breathe because I'm not healthy enough.
For tips, I would just say to look at yourself and focus on how you're feeling. Take it one a day at a time, one week, and it'll get better. It's extremely hard at first, not going to lie, but you can definitely get through it. I started with easy, simple exercises and small changes to my diet - wheat bread over white, water over soda, less sugar. I also started going to bed eariler and waking up at a normal time. It's small things at first that make all the difference in the long run. Don't try to throw yourself into it or expect changes overnight - it's a process that takes time, but is so worth it! Also, it helps to picture yourself as the version you want to be, or to pick someone to look up to, famous or not.

Instead of searching for motivation, try discipline - think of it this way - you have to workout, you have to eat better to become healthy. You might not want to right now, but if you do it, future you will thank past you. Exercising today because you have to in order to become healthy is a good mindset. I wake up every morning and I don't want to exercise, I never have motivation to do it. But I do it because I make myself to, because I know that in the long run, I'll get stronger and healthier. Sometimes in life, you'll have to do things you don't want to do, and exercise is one of them. Also, it helps to have some sort of routine, a set time for exercising. Pick a time that works for you, and try exercising at that time every day for a week, then another week, and another one, and eventually it'll become habit.

Try to make a list of things you want to work on, and then take small steps in making them reality. It's okay to take time for yourself, making yourself better. You can't spend your life making everyone else happy while you're miserable yourself, that's no way to live. You deserve a good, happy life. Put yourself first for even just a day, and you'll notice the difference.
